A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same pruning-activated attack, with matching authors, method, and core experiments. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, and equations, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original attack-success and utility measurements across five language models, three attack scenarios, and multiple pruning configurations, plus ablations and defense experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds experiments on larger models, post-pruning transformations, injection-size sensitivity, and calibration-domain shifts.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 and Algorithm 1 retain Wanda-based score estimation, injection into high-scoring parameters, repair through low-scoring parameters, and the same losses. Correcting percentage-complement expressions does not change the already specified freezing procedure; the new experiments do not introduce an attack component.

E1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds reasoning-domain calibration scenarios using GSM8K question-answer/reasoning pairs and OpenPlatypus, extending the original C4-to-WikiText calibration mismatch. The three attack tasks and five utility benchmarks remain unchanged; GSM8K's new role is calibration rather than an additional utility benchmark.

E2.justification: Figure 4 adds evaluated mitigation comparisons using sparse fine-tuning on general instruction data alone versus general plus security data. The base-model comparisons in Table 2 and the existing security-aware calibration and patching comparisons in Tables 3–4 are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include Qwen2.5-14B/32B evaluation, sparsity-preserving fine-tuning with a 1:1 general/security-data mixture, and FP8 or 4-bit GPTQ after pruning. Figure 10 varies injection fractions across 20%, 50%, and 80%, while Figure 2 extends the repair sweep to 0.1%. These substantially expand experimental settings without changing the retained main attack setup.

E4.justification: Section 6.4 newly tests whether attacks survive subsequent fine-tuning and quantization, including targeted security fine-tuning as mitigation. Appendix B.1 adds injection-fraction sensitivity and reasoning-calibration distribution-shift analyses, while Figure 2 extends the existing repair-fraction ablation. These address several previously untested robustness questions.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly reports mean benchmark-score changes with standard deviations across the five benchmarks, replacing absolute averages. This adds descriptive variability reporting, not repeated-run uncertainty. Neither version reports additional seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 5–7 and Figures 4 and 10 add substantial ASR and utility results, including suppression through security fine-tuning and persistence after quantization. Table 2 is unchanged. Table 1 corrects summaries, including Llama's benign-refusal rate from 0.8% to 3.9%, and v3 Table 11 corrects the model assignments of result blocks in v1 Table 8; these corrections do not establish rerun performance changes.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the frozen-parameter complements from (1 − alpha)% to (100 − alpha)% for injection and repair, resolving an arithmetic inconsistency with percentage-valued alpha. The pruning-score derivation and algorithmic update equations remain unchanged; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: the first pruning-activated LLM attack, benign behavior before pruning, malicious activation afterward, and a deployment-time security gap. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining their stated scope.

C2.justification: Section 6.4 adds a substantive qualification: security-data fine-tuning can mitigate the attack, but requires identifying the compromise and curating appropriate data. Appendix B.1 interprets calibration-domain shifts as insufficient for reliable protection despite reduced SparseGPT ASR. Existing mechanism explanations and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.4 documents the existing security-aware calibration experiment: 512 sequences, approximately 2048 tokens each, formed by concatenating five query/refusal pairs from roughly 2.5k LLM-LAT entries, with an example in Figure 9. V3 also specifies settings for the new transformation experiments. These additions improve documentation; the original attack hyperparameters and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: V3 adds references to GPTQ (Frantar et al., 2022) and Platypus (Lee et al., 2023) for the new experiments. Section 2's research positioning remains essentially unchanged. Numerous other reference edits change metadata or publication versions of already cited works.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative order remain intact. V3 adds Sections 6.4, A.4, and B.1, moves the full-results subsection to B.2, makes localized wording corrections, updates publication headers and bibliography formatting, and removes the acknowledgements containing a drafting note. This is a bounded structural expansion rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with clearer pruning options and illustrative responses, Table 1 is redesigned around score changes and standard deviations, and Figure 2 gains an extended axis and additional points. New Figures 4, 9, and 10 and Tables 5–7 substantially expand the visual presentation beyond renumbering or relocation.

improvement.justification: V3 resolves important reporting inconsistencies in the utility summary and model attribution of content-injection results, improving the reliability of the evidence. The added transformation and calibration-shift tests strengthen its practical assessment, while Figure 4 provides an empirically supported, explicitly qualified mitigation. Together these substantially improve trustworthiness and usefulness. Several new tests remain limited to Qwen, and the added standard deviations do not establish repeated-run uncertainty.
